scope: disambiguate netchan.remoteAddress by requiring port 29000 next to 127.0.0.1

verified_facts.forward_bound_port: Get-NetUDPEndpoint shows LocalPort 29000 owned by the bridge process
verified_facts.dedrun_bound_port: Get-NetUDPEndpoint shows LocalPort 28970 owned by codol_dedrun
verified_facts.hit_interpretation: the only 127.0.0.1 occurrence is followed by 00 00 00 00, i.e. port 0, so it cannot be the endpoint the dedrun sends to (the bridge listens on 29000)
verified_facts.disambiguation_result: requiring port 29000 produced adr_address 0x0 and outgoing_sequence 0, so the scan found nothing
verified_facts.server: no AdministraClient out line after the change; last known line before it was state 2 / ack 0 / gamestate -1

inference_not_verified.statement: the single hit is probably a different address field in client_t (port 0), and netchan.remoteAddress is either outside base-0x8000 or stores a different ip representation
inference_not_verified.basis: only one 127.0.0.1 pattern exists in that window and its port is 0
inference_not_verified.how_to_check: walk the client_t field layout from the source (name at +0x2B8, netchan at line 134 of server.h) and read netchan at a computed offset instead of scanning bytes

unknown: the exact offset of netchan inside client_t for this build
whether netchan.remoteAddress holds 127.0.0.1 at all after the rewrite through NET_CompareAdr
next: compute client_t field sizes from server.h between netchan (line 134) and name (+0x2B8) to get netchan's offset, then read netchan+0x10 as remoteAddress and netchan+0x00 as outgoingSequence
